title: General knowledge sampler
desc: A short set to try QBank: single answer, select all that apply, and true or false.

questions.stem: The diagram shows the Sun and the four planets that orbit nearest to it.
questions.ask: Which planet is number 1 in the diagram?

images.alt: The Sun and four planets on their orbits, numbered 1 to 4 from the nearest orbit outward
images.caption: Not to scale
images.svg: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='340' height='200' viewBox='0 0 340 200' font-family='-apple-system, Helvetica, sans-serif'><rect width='340' height='200' fill='#ffffff'/><circle cx='66' cy='100' r='52' fill='none' stroke='#94a3b8' stroke-width='1.5' stroke-dasharray='4 4'/><path d='M95 -8 A112 112 0 0 1 95 208' fill='none' stroke='#94a3b8' stroke-width='1.5' stroke-dasharray='4 4'/><path d='M111 -66 A172 172 0 0 1 111 266' fill='none' stroke='#94a3b8' stroke-width='1.5' stroke-dasharray='4 4'/><path d='M126 -124 A232 232 0 0 1 126 324' fill='none' stroke='#94a3b8' stroke-width='1.5' stroke-dasharray='4 4'/><circle cx='66' cy='100' r='20' fill='#f59e0b'/><text x='66' y='138' font-size='13' font-weight='600' text-anchor='middle' fill='#1f2937'>Sun</text><circle cx='107' cy='68' r='6' fill='#6b7280'/><text x='107' y='55' font-size='16' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' fill='#111827' stroke='#ffffff' stroke-width='4' paint-order='stroke'>1</text><circle cx='168' cy='146' r='9' fill='#d97706'/><text x='168' y='130' font-size='16' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' fill='#111827' stroke='#ffffff' stroke-width='4' paint-order='stroke'>2</text><circle cx='230' cy='50' r='10' fill='#2563eb'/><text x='230' y='33' font-size='16' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' fill='#111827' stroke='#ffffff' stroke-width='4' paint-order='stroke'>3</text><circle cx='295' cy='136' r='8' fill='#dc2626'/><text x='295' y='121' font-size='16' font-weight='700' text-anchor='middle' fill='#111827' stroke='#ffffff' stroke-width='4' paint-order='stroke'>4</text></svg>

questions.rationale: Number 1 is on the innermost orbit. Mercury orbits closest to the Sun, about 58 million kilometers away. Number 2 is Venus, 3 is Earth and 4 is Mars.
questions.takeaway: The order from the Sun is Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

questions.stem: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
questions.ask: Is the statement true or false?
questions.rationale: At standard sea-level air pressure, pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius. Where the air pressure is lower, such as on a high mountain, it boils at a lower temperature.
questions.takeaway: The boiling point of water depends on air pressure.

questions.stem: A shop takes 15% off an item that costs 80 dollars.
questions.ask: How many dollars does the discount take off?

images.alt: A bar standing for 80 dollars, with 10 percent marked as 8 and a further 5 percent marked as 4
images.caption: 15% of 80, built from two easy pieces
images.svg: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='340' height='150' viewBox='0 0 340 150' font-family='-apple-system, Helvetica, sans-serif' font-size='14' fill='#111827'><rect width='340' height='150' fill='#ffffff'/><text x='170' y='22' text-anchor='middle' font-weight='600'>The whole bar is 80 dollars</text><rect x='10' y='60' width='32' height='36' fill='#2563eb'/><rect x='42' y='60' width='16' height='36' fill='#f59e0b'/><rect x='58' y='60' width='272' height='36' fill='#e5e7eb'/><rect x='10' y='60' width='320' height='36' fill='none' stroke='#374151' stroke-width='1.5'/><path d='M26 60 V46' stroke='#374151' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='10' y='42'>10% = 8</text><path d='M50 96 V112' stroke='#374151' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='32' y='128'>5% = 4</text><text x='194' y='83' text-anchor='middle'>85% still to pay</text><text x='330' y='128' text-anchor='end' font-weight='700'>15% = 8 + 4 = 12</text></svg>

questions.rationale: 10% of 80 is 8 and 5% of 80 is 4, so 15% is 8 + 4 = 12.
questions.takeaway: Build a percentage from easy pieces: 10%, then half of that for 5%.

questions.stem: Mammals are warm-blooded animals that feed their young with milk.
questions.ask: Which of these animals are mammals? Select all that apply.
questions.rationale: Dolphins, bats and kangaroos are mammals. Sharks are fish and penguins are birds, and neither feeds its young with milk.
questions.takeaway: Living in the sea or flying does not decide the group; feeding young with milk does.

questions.stem: The Earth's surface is mostly water, divided into five named oceans.
questions.ask: Which ocean is the largest by area?
questions.rationale: The Pacific Ocean covers about a third of the Earth's surface, more than all of the land together.
questions.takeaway: Largest to smallest: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic.

questions.stem: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
questions.ask: Is the statement true or false?
questions.rationale: Lightning often strikes the same place again. Tall, pointed structures are hit many times a year.
questions.takeaway: A saying can sound sure and still be wrong; check the facts.

questions.stem: A synonym is a word with nearly the same meaning as another word.
questions.ask: Which word is a synonym of "brief"?
questions.rationale: "Brief" means lasting a short time, so "short" is the closest match. "Lengthy" is its opposite.
questions.takeaway: Test a synonym by swapping it into the sentence and checking the meaning holds.

questions.stem: Research on learning compares many ways of studying.
questions.ask: Which habits help you remember what you study? Select all that apply.

options.t: Spreading study sessions over several days
Testing yourself without looking at your notes
Rereading the same page again and again in one sitting
Highlighting every line of a page
Explaining an idea in your own words

questions.rationale: Spacing sessions, testing yourself and explaining ideas in your own words all make memories stronger. Rereading and highlighting feel productive, but they do much less.
questions.takeaway: Practicing questions, as in this app, is itself one of the best ways to learn.

questions.stem: In the 15th century, printing with movable metal type spread across Europe.
questions.ask: Which person is best known for introducing it there?
questions.rationale: Johannes Gutenberg built a printing press with movable metal type in the 1450s, which made books far cheaper to produce.
questions.takeaway: Cheaper books helped ideas spread to many more readers.

questions.stem: Spaced repetition is a way of reviewing material.

options.t: Reviewing the same material again after longer and longer gaps
Reading all of the material once, very slowly
Studying only on the night before a test
Leaving a blank line between every note

questions.rationale: Each review comes just as the memory starts to fade, so every pass makes it last longer.
questions.takeaway: Short reviews spread over time beat one long session.
